memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Every grain offering you bring to the LORD must be made without yeast, for you must not burn any yeast or honey in a food offering presented to the LORD.'" - Lev 2:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Yeast we understand — it pictures corruption spreading quietly. But honey? Honey is good. Scripture calls the Promised Land a land flowing with milk and honey. God's words are said to be sweeter than honey (Ps 19:10).

So why keep it off the altar?

The most likely reason is that honey, like yeast, causes fermentation. Both make dough rise and sour over time. Both introduce change that God did not want in what represented Him.

But there may be a gentler lesson too. Not everything sweet belongs on the altar. Some things are genuinely good gifts from God — pleasures, comforts, enjoyments — that are simply not what worship is made of. Worship is not sweetened to our taste. We do not add honey to make God more palatable.

There is a modern temptation to present a version of faith that goes down easily, all comfort and no cost, all encouragement and no repentance. Paul warned Timothy about a time when people would gather teachers who say what their itching ears want to hear (2 Tim 4:3).

God is not asking us to be joyless. He is asking that our worship be true rather than sweetened.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I want a version of God that suits my taste, or the God who actually is?
2. Have I avoided parts of Scripture because they are not sweet?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from a faith I have flavoured to suit myself. Give me appetite for the truth as You have given it. Amen.
